records.title: Causally valid two-candidate authority selection
records.hypothesis: A final decision interface can use a late authority cue to select between two candidate operations when trained end to end.
records.result: All four S4 arms reached 40/40 validation selection, 20/20 counterfactual flips and 20/20 paired correctness, including the unseen layout.
limits: Two candidates
Synthetic authority cue
Does not establish arbitrary instruction hierarchy or autonomous reasoning

records.title: D2 component ablation
records.hypothesis: The S4 improvement is attributable to candidate-slot readout and/or decision-only training rather than the original D2 configuration.
records.result: C1, C2 and C3 all passed; C4 remained below training competence. Operation-class decision-only was sufficient in the two-candidate task, but C4 was historical and not retrained under the crossed-cell trajectory.
limits: C4 is a reused historical checkpoint

records.title: Dynamic shared scoring for compositional authority transfer
records.hypothesis: A shared query/candidate scorer will transfer authority selection from three candidates to four candidates and unseen layouts.
records.result: The gate achieved 72/120 four-candidate pointer accuracy and 0/24 paired counterfactual correctness. Abstention was 24/24; positional transfer was poor and relation matching was partial.

Does not prove shared scoring impossible

records.title: Explicit candidate-ID matching across cardinalities
records.hypothesis: Separating candidate-ID extraction from matching will reveal whether shared scoring can transfer across 2/3 to 4/5/8 candidates.
interventions: Matched fixed-slot head versus shared scorer
records.result: The deterministic oracle passed 2064/2064 rows. None of the eight learned arms passed the 95% training gate: fixed-slot arms reached 384--388/576 and shared-scorer arms 444--497/576. Learned transfer is therefore not interpretable.

Does not show that shared scoring is impossible

records.hypothesis: Explicit authority-pointer supervision will transfer operation authority selection to unseen competing-cue layouts.
records.result: A3 learned all operand and operation pointers on training rows and reached 32/32 on authority-near, authority-early and authority-middle pooled layouts, but achieved 4/32 on reversed authority and 4/32 on conflicting cues. The oracle achieved 32/32 on every layout.

records.title: Corrected authority-aware role binding rerun
records.hypothesis: Balanced explicit authority-pointer supervision will achieve transferable authority selection on unseen conflicting-operation examples.
records.result: A3 passed the training pointer gate in all four arms (240/240 pointer tuples per run), but the primary unseen conflicting-cue criterion was 2/32 paired groups (6.25%). Operand pointers were 80/80 while authority pointers were 40/80 on those rows; the oracle was 32/32 on every layout.

records.hypothesis: Changing only the authority designation will reverse the learned operation pointer.
interventions: Read-only fixed-width authority swap on A3 checkpoints
records.result: The A3 pointer changed on 0/160 counterfactual pairs in every listed layout. The export contained 326 invalid-format rows because LATER padding introduced a surface form absent from v2 training; the position-safe raw-label v2 result is the accepted diagnostic.

records.title: Position-safe raw-label authority counterfactual
records.hypothesis: The A3 parser will change its selected operation when EARLIER/LATER authority is reversed in a position-safe unseen layout.
records.result: Correct pointer flips were 0/160 and correct unequal-output flips were 0/128. The pointer was unchanged for every counterfactual pair; selected-operation accuracy was 116/160 for EARLIER and 44/160 for LATER, reflecting a static preference rather than authority sensitivity.

records.hypothesis: The late authority cue may be represented while remaining unavailable to earlier operation-pointer states.
records.result: Authority-token probes reached 100% across tested domains, while operation-position probes were only 40/80 in the unseen reversed layout. Changing authority produced 0/80 pointer changes and 0 hidden/logit change at operation positions in each model, consistent with causal inaccessibility of later information at earlier states.

records.hypothesis: Batch composition or update ordering is a primary cause of conditional-execution training failure.
interventions: Diverse/same-pair batch composition crossed with shuffled/grouped ordering
records.result: Diverse grouped training improved mean fit over diverse shuffled training, while same-pair grouped training was worse than same-pair shuffled training. The best held-out paired results were only 16/32, and gradient cosine was descriptive rather than causal evidence of interference.

records.title: Causally valid authority decision placement
records.hypothesis: A decision made after the authority cue, or with authority placed before candidate pointers, can learn authority-conditioned selection.
records.result: D1 reached 80/80 paired training, 80/80 paired validation and 20/20 validation operation flips. D0 and D2 failed training competence; D2 therefore remains an unresolved readout-learning failure rather than evidence against post-context access.

records.hypothesis: The original four failing operand pairs are persistent pair-specific weaknesses rather than artifacts of one split.
records.result: Held-out equal operands were 0/32 while held-out non-diagonal pairs were 133/208; trained diagonal observations were 47/48 correct. The original four failures moved with the partition, while the held-out diagonal failure persisted under these splits.

records.hypothesis: Held-out equal-operand pairs are harder than matched unequal pairs, independent of the original split.
interventions: Diagonal, mixed and matched-unequal special holdouts

records.hypothesis: The joint role-selection failure is caused by missing operation representation, conditional routing, gradient interference, binding, or an operation-blind shortcut.

records.title: Single-token operation-marker intervention
records.hypothesis: Replacing multi-byte operation words with length-preserving one-byte markers will restore joint conditional execution.

records.hypothesis: Moving the operation field to a fixed answer-boundary position will restore instruction-conditioned execution, with encoding and position separable in a small matrix.

records.hypothesis: The frozen dense model can identify SELECT_FIRST versus SELECT_SECOND as an explicit operation class.

records.hypothesis: Grouping equivalent positional variants, with or without a consistency loss, will improve position-generalized conditional execution.
records.result: A0 achieved 96.88--100% training paired performance and 53.12--59.38% held-out paired rates. A1/A2 fit only 47.50--57.92% and had 0--3.12% held-out paired performance. The proposed grouping and consistency intervention did not help under this protocol.

records.hypothesis: Training across fixed-near, early and middle instruction positions will produce position-robust conditional execution.
records.result: The fixed control reached 100% paired training and 100% paired accuracy on adjacent layouts, while the position-varied intervention had 27--32/32 training paired competence and 0/32 paired performance on every reported held-out layout, including familiar layouts; one intervention arm failed the fit gate.

records.hypothesis: A model trained with an answer-adjacent instruction will lose conditional execution when the instruction is moved or surrounded by unfamiliar context.
records.result: Frozen A3 paired accuracy was 90.62% adjacent, 50% near with padding and 0% early with padding. The explicit authority cue variant was also 0%; the tested competing variant stayed 90.62%. Instrumentation reproduced native logits within 1.43e-05.

interventions: Corrected native-SDPA output plus shadow Q/K summaries

The passing cyclic arms reached 70/96 and 81/96 validation accuracy, with perfect abstention but only 9/32 and 17/32 paired validation groups.

records.title: Two-candidate transfer forensics: candidate regime by serialization
records.hypothesis: The accepted two-candidate validation gap is primarily caused by input-layout shift, candidate-pair recombination, or their interaction.
interventions: Checkpoint-only 2x2 crossing familiar/recombined candidate sets with compact/padded serialization
records.result: Familiar candidate sets remained perfect in both compact and padded serialization for both seeds. Recombined candidate sets remained impaired in compact serialization, close to padded validation performance: seed 42 75/96 and 11/32 paired groups; seed 1337 80/96 and 16/32. The result weakens a padding-only explanation but cannot isolate candidate-set recombination from the original operand-context shift.

records.title: Matched-context familiar versus recombined candidate-set probe
records.hypothesis: If familiar candidate sets outperform recombined candidate sets on the same source operand contexts, the transfer gap is not explained solely by the original operand-context shift.
interventions: Checkpoint-only evaluation of both candidate regimes on identical training-source and validation-source context strata
records.result: Both seeds were perfect on familiar candidate sets in both context strata: 240/240 rows and 80/80 paired groups overall. Recombined candidate sets were lower in both strata: seed 42 111/144 on training-source contexts and 75/96 on validation-source contexts; seed 1337 121/144 and 80/96. The matched contrast is therefore consistent with a candidate-set-regime effect under these checkpoint-only probes.

records.title: Two-candidate identifier and reversal forensics
records.hypothesis: Existing errors can distinguish exact candidate-pair association, fixed-slot bias, target-slot bias and a more general but imperfect matching rule.
interventions: Post-hoc ordered-pair, unordered-pair, target-slot, predicted-identity and reversal analysis of committed matrices
records.result: Recombined errors were concentrated in unordered pairs rather than spread uniformly: `(2,5)` and `(3,6)` failed persistently in both seeds, `(0,3)` was perfect in both and `(1,4)` was seed-dependent. All recombined abstentions were correct. Reversal usually preserved predicted identity and flipped slot; 23/80 seed-42 and 19/80 seed-1337 reversal groups were both wrong with the same identity. The data support a pair-specific behavioral weakness but do not prove memorization or a mechanism.

records.title: Rotated two-candidate unordered-pair coverage
records.hypothesis: Rotating disjoint unordered candidate-pair holdouts will distinguish held-out pair coverage from a persistent identifier-family weakness after training competence is established.
interventions: Dense SHARED_SCORER cyclic training with 500 updates
records.result: All 8/8 arms reached 144/144 training accuracy. Pooled validation was 656/768 rows (85.42%), 144/256 paired groups (56.25%) and 256/256 abstention rows (100%). The four held-out panels produced 47/64, 32/64, 33/64 and 32/64 paired groups respectively, with a strong partition-by-seed interaction: P1 was 1/32 versus 32/32 and P2 was 32/32 versus 0/32. The result establishes a held-out pair-transfer gap with seed sensitivity, but not a persistent identifier-family mechanism.

records.title: Two-candidate training-partner crossover
records.hypothesis: For a fixed held-out candidate-pair panel, transfer performance changes with the training-partner panel, distinguishing coverage-graph dependence from a persistent single-pair weakness.
interventions: 16 new dense SHARED_SCORER cyclic arms combined with 8 immutable prior arms
controls: Three training partners per held-out panel
records.result: All 16 new and all 24 combined arms passed training competence. Combined validation was 2,031/2,304 rows (88.15%), 495/768 paired groups (64.45%) and 768/768 abstention rows (100%). For held-out M0, M2 training produced 0/64 paired groups across both seeds, while M1 and M3 training each produced 47/64. No unordered pair was zero across its six crossover evaluations. The data support training-partner/coverage-graph dependence under this task and retain seed sensitivity, without establishing a neural mechanism.

records.title: Two-candidate nested coverage-density transfer
records.hypothesis: At a fixed 144-row training budget, increasing the number of distinct training candidate pairs improves transfer to one fixed unseen candidate panel.
records.result: The four new D8/D12 arms produced three training-gate passes: D8 seed 42 reached 120/144 and failed, D8 seed 1337 reached 138/144 and passed, and both D12 seeds reached 144/144. The immutable D4 references both passed. Fixed-M2 validation was 80/96 and 95/96 for D4, 67/96 and 77/96 for D8, and 64/96 and 72/96 for D12; abstention was 32/32 in every arm. The run does not support a simple monotonic coverage benefit under this fixed-row design, but the D4/D8/D12 conditions also change per-pair repetition, degree and connectivity.

records.title: Matched-degree relational topology control
records.hypothesis: Holding identifier exposure, degree, edge count, training budget and evaluation identities constant, changing graph topology and shortest-path structure changes transfer on an explicitly path-compositional edge-offset task.
interventions: P12_PRISM versus R12_DIAMETER5 matched-degree graph families
fixed held-out unordered node pairs and both query directions
controls: independent post-run hash and data audit
records.result: The graph and oracle controls passed. Only 1/4 arms passed the 95% training gate: P12_PRISM seed 42 reached 139/144 (96.5%), while P12_PRISM seed 1337 reached 135/144, R12_DIAMETER5 seed 42 reached 123/144 and R12_DIAMETER5 seed 1337 reached 125/144. The gated P12 arm achieved 59/96 value-correct validation rows and 19/48 paired groups, but no diameter-5 arm was training-competent. records.title: Symbolic topology and effective-resistance audit
records.hypothesis: The proposed graph-structural, diffusion, modular-oracle and effective-resistance mechanisms can be independently reproduced, and their pair-level predictions can be tested against the committed topology checkpoints.
interventions: pair-level distance/resistance/bridge analysis of four checkpoints
records.result: The structural claims and random-regular control reproduced: the diameter-5 graph has a bridge, lower algebraic connectivity and higher held-out effective resistance, while diameter-5 graphs without bridges also exist. The modular path oracle was 100% for both graphs across all tested moduli. Effective-resistance formulae matched independent global least-squares noise simulations. Baseline neural pair errors did not consistently track shortest-path distance, effective resistance or bridge crossing; pair 0–9 improved under the diameter-5 graph in both seeds, but the eight-pair design cannot separate competing predictors and three original arms failed training competence.

records.title: Constructive shared latent-potential relational baseline
records.hypothesis: A supplied shared latent-potential representation can compose unseen modular node relationships across the committed topology graphs, while a lookup baseline cannot.
records.result: The supplied latent-potential composition recovered 24,000/24,000 held-out relations for each graph across all three moduli. Random lookup stayed near its expected 1/K accuracy. After one random ±1 edge corruption, shortest-path accuracy was 84.96%, 85.49% and 86.04% for the prism and 80.89%, 82.40% and 82.53% for the diameter-5 graph at K=5, 11 and 97 respectively. Uncorrupted edge consistency passed every trial; corrupted-cycle inconsistency was detected on every prism trial and on the non-bridge fraction of diameter-5 trials.

records.title: Topology-control training-duration extension
records.hypothesis: The original topology-control training-gate failures may reflect slower acquisition rather than an inability to learn the observed edge-offset task under the frozen recipe.
interventions: Exact four-arm retraining from fresh initialization for 2,000 updates
controls: Same optimizer, batch size, cyclic schedule and seeds
records.result: All four arms passed the final 95% training gate after 2,000 updates. P12_PRISM reached 142/144 and 143/144 training rows for seeds 42 and 1337; R12_DIAMETER5 reached 141/144 and 143/144. The first recorded gate was step 500 for P12 seed 42 and step 750 for the other three arms. Final validation was P12 72/96 and 59/96, D5 62/96 and 51/96, with paired correctness 29/48, 23/48, 18/48 and 16/48 respectively. Independent audit reproduced all 500-step baseline metrics and recomputed every final CSV metric.

records.title: Learned shared-latent neural relational transfer
records.hypothesis: A parameter-matched neural model with shared relational representations will learn the edge-offset task to competence and transfer better than the frozen dense scorer; an auxiliary cycle-consistency objective will improve that transfer.
interventions: N2 shared graph latent states plus preregistered cycle loss
2,000-step cyclic training on both topology families and both seeds
records.result: All eight implemented N1/N2 arms passed the 95% training gate. Matched paired validation was N0 86/192 (44.8%), N1 59/192 (30.7%) and N2 53/192 (27.6%). No N1 or N2 arm exceeded N0 in its matched cell, so neither the shared-latent improvement criterion nor the cycle-consistency benefit criterion was met. A read-only checkpoint replay verified the committed predictions and found N1/N2 preserved predicted value across every candidate-order counterfactual (48/48 per arm) while often preserving the wrong value; this is descriptive evidence of order-invariant failure, not a unique causal mechanism.
limits: N1/N2 receive a structured parsed edge representation while N0 is a raw byte-sequence scorer, so the comparison is not a pure architectural ablation
Two graph families and two seeds
Known-identifier held-out pairs only
Identifier-renaming and entirely unseen-identifier transfer were not executed
A negative result for these configurations does not prove shared latent representations or cycle consistency impossible in general
The protocol cost paragraph said four new arms while the implemented matrix contained eight; all eight are reported and audited
unresolved: Whether a different structured representation or query readout can transfer
Whether cycle consistency can help with a stable loss and an appropriate readout
Whether a neural model can learn the supplied symbolic latent-potential procedure under a better-matched interface
Whether transfer extends to identifier renaming or entirely unseen identifiers

records.title: Engineered procedural learning lifecycle v0
records.hypothesis: A bounded procedural learner can acquire an undisclosed rule from demonstrations, verify it independently, persist the procedure across a temporary-context reset, execute it on unseen inputs and revise it after contradictory evidence.
records.result: All 24/24 tasks were acquired and independently verified. The reloaded learner executed 288/288 post-reset queries correctly with 100% coverage. No-persistence and raw-example controls had 0/288 coverage after reset; 18/24 insufficient-evidence tasks remained uncertain; 24/24 contradictory-demonstrations controls were not promoted; revision invalidated version 1 and produced validated version 2.
limits: The eight-rule hypothesis family is supplied and hard-coded
Candidate filtering, probe selection and execution are deterministic
The oracle supplies active-probe and verification outputs
Contradiction invalidation is externally invoked by the benchmark rather than independently detected
Scaffolding was not measured before this audit
No neural adaptation or held-out procedure family was tested
unresolved: Whether a learned proposer can replace candidate induction without reducing lifecycle reliability
Whether the proposer can operate over withheld procedure families
Whether contradiction detection can be learned separately
How scaffolding dependence should be measured across versions

records.title: Track B C1 engineered acquisition, reuse and evidence-control series
records.hypothesis: Bounded controllers can safely acquire, reuse, adapt, verify and revise procedures or strategy records across sequential tasks while controlling harmful transfer and evidence uncertainty.
records.result: The series provides reusable engineered-controller evidence: safe adaptive policies can reduce cost while abstaining under several synthetic uncertainty conditions, while naive persistence can cause harmful transfer. Active evidence and counterexample refinement improve conditional reliability in their bounded environments. The series does not establish a neural model acquiring and retaining an executable procedure through the Lifecycle v0 interface.
limits: The experiments have heterogeneous task generators and objectives
Most procedures, memory policies and verifiers are engineered
Results are not a single end-to-end lifecycle gate
No neural procedure proposer was trained
Some follow-ons preserve known synthetic task structure
Aggregate series status cannot replace individual report interpretation
unresolved: Whether a learned proposer can replace deterministic induction
Whether engineered safe reuse transfers to a neural lifecycle
Whether scaffolding can be reduced without increasing harmful transfer
Whether contradiction detection can be initiated by the learner

records.title: Digitwise addition ladder read-only checkpoint forensics
records.hypothesis: Read-only reproduction and per-pair analysis can separate evaluator/output-format effects from the observed held-out arithmetic errors without retraining.
records.result: Both read-only forensic reports reproduced the original metrics and separated digit, EOS and full-sequence errors. The v3 analysis found common validation pair failures but no output-format or EOS failure; pair-level and split-membership effects remain descriptive on the small corpus.
limits: Read-only analysis cannot establish a causal mechanism
Small fixed validation set
Pair identity and split membership remain confounded
No new training or architecture evidence
unresolved: Whether pair-specific errors persist under repeated balanced holdouts
Whether the arithmetic failure is relevant to the Track B learner boundary
